title: Relative flatness through an etale diagram and a closed support
statement: Let $X,S,U,T,Z$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with morphisms $f:X\to S$, $a:U\to T$, $g:U\to X$, $e:T\to S$ satisfying $fg=ea$. Assume $g$ and $e$ are etale [def-weil-etale-morphism], and $i:Z\hookrightarrow U$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Let $\mathcal F$ and $\mathcal G$ be quasi-coherent modules on $X$ and $Z$, respectively [pqf-def-coherent], and fix an $\mathcal O_U$-linear isomorphism $H:=g^*\mathcal F\cong i_*\mathcal G$, with pullback and pushforward as in [def-pc-module-pullback]. For $z\in Z$, put $u=i(z)$, $x=g(u)$, $t=a(u)$, and $s=e(t)=f(x)$. Relative flatness is as in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over], with structure maps $f$, $a$, and $ai$. Then the following three neighbourhood conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ on an open neighbourhood of $x$; $H$ is flat over $T$ on an open neighbourhood of $u$; $\mathcal G$ is flat over $T$ on an open neighbourhood of $z$. Separately, the following three stalk conditions are equivalent: $\mathcal F_x$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,s}$; $H_u$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$; $\mathcal G_z$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Stalks [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] carry the scalar actions induced by the displayed structure maps. No cartesian-square, affineness, finite-type, finite-presentation, residue-field-isomorphism or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: First obtain a comparison at every point $w\in U$, writing $v=g(w)$, $r=a(w)$ and $b=f(v)=e(r)$. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-quasi-coherent], $H=g^*\mathcal F$ is quasi-coherent. Etaleness includes flatness by [def-weil-etale-morphism], so [lem-trf-relative-flatness-source-cover], applied to $U\xrightarrow{g}X\xrightarrow{f}S$, gives $\mathcal F_v$ flat over $\mathcal O_{S,b}$ if and only if $H_w$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{S,b}$. Apply [lem-trf-etale-local-ring-flatness] to $e:T\to S$, $r\in T$, and the $\mathcal O_{T,r}$-module $H_w$ with action through $a$. It identifies the latter condition with flatness over $\mathcal O_{T,r}$. The restricted action is exactly the action through $fg$, since $fg=ea$. Thus these pointwise equivalences hold for every $w$, without a cartesian-square assumption.

proof.text: Use the stalk characterization in [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. If $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ on an open $V\ni x$, then $g^{-1}(V)$ is open and contains $u$; Step 1 at every point of this inverse image shows $H$ flat over $T$ there. Conversely, if $H$ is flat over $T$ on an open $W\ni u$, then $g(W)$ is an open neighbourhood of $x$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-morphism-open-map]. Every $v\in g(W)$ has a preimage $w\in W$, so Step 1 shows $\mathcal F_v$ flat over $\mathcal O_{S,f(v)}$. Thus $\mathcal F$ is flat over $S$ throughout $g(W)$. This proves the first two neighbourhood conditions equivalent; no deduction of neighbourhood flatness from flatness at just one point is made.

source.place: Tag 057U, lemma-devissage-flat, paragraph using openness of g and Morphisms Tag 02JZ; Morphisms Tag 03WT, lemma-etale-open.

proof.text: A closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its closed image by [def-weil-closed-immersion], so [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks] applies to $i$ and $\mathcal G$. At each $q\in Z$ it gives a bijective $\mathcal O_{U,i(q)}$-linear germ map $(i_*\mathcal G)_{i(q)}\to\mathcal G_q$, with the action on the right through $i^\sharp_q$, and it gives a zero stalk at every point outside $i(Z)$. Apply the stalk functor [def-pc-module-stalk-functor] to the given isomorphism $H\cong i_*\mathcal G$ and its inverse. Composing with the germ map identifies $H_{i(q)}$ with $\mathcal G_q$, linearly over $\mathcal O_{T,a(i(q))}$: a scalar acts on the right through $i^\sharp_q a^\sharp_{i(q)}=(ai)^\sharp_q$. Hence their flatness over this same base local ring is equivalent. Indeed, tensoring an injection with isomorphic modules gives conjugate maps, so injectivity is unchanged by [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; the zero module is flat since tensoring with it gives the zero map between zero modules. Thus the marked stalk conditions for $H_u$ and $\mathcal G_z$ are equivalent, and $H_w$ is flat over the base local ring for every $w\notin i(Z)$.

i z$ in $Z$. The subspace-topology clause of [def-weil-closed-immersion] supplies an open $V\subseteq U$ with $i^{-1}(V)=W$; it contains $u=i(z)$. At every point of $V\cap i(Z)$, Step 3 transfers flatness from the corresponding stalk of $\mathcal G$, and at every point of $V\setminus i(Z)$ the stalk of $H$ is zero and flat by Step 3. The stalk characterization therefore shows $H$ flat over $T$ on $V$. This proves the last two neighbourhood conditions equivalent.

source.place: Tag 057U, lemma-devissage-flat, closed-support part of (4) versus (2); topological shrinking written out using the closed embedding and the stalk calculation of Step 3.

proof.text: Steps 2 and 4 give all three neighbourhood conditions equivalent by transitivity. Specializing Step 1 to $w=u$ compares $\mathcal F_x$ with $H_u$, with base points $s$ and $t$ as in the statement. Step 3 at $q=z$ compares $H_u$ with $\mathcal G_z$ over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$. Transitivity gives the separate three-way stalk equivalence. These are two separate equivalence assertions; none of the steps identifies flatness at a single stalk with flatness on a neighbourhood.

Neighbourhood flatness is never inferred from flatness at a single point. Step 3: the closed-pushforward-stalks node (Lean sorry-free) gives zero stalks off i(Z) and an O_{U,i(q)}-linear germ bijection. Restricting along a^♯ gives O_T-linearity through (ai)^♯. Step 4: the subspace-topology choice W=i^{-1}(V) is correct, and openness of i(Z)∩V is not needed. Step 5: transitivity. Edge cases tested: empty Z, identity maps, the non-flat closed immersion Spec F_2→Spec Z, and étale maps with residue-field extensions. The parent elementary-devissage-flatness uses the item consistently: it inverts the isomorphism and has ai=hπ.
